sheet-9999997-1.description: The main map of the one-sheet Oakhurst atlas (sheet 73 of the 1907 New Jersey Coast volume one), drawn at 60 feet to an inch. It covers the village centre along Main Street, also labelled Monmouth Road, which runs straight down the sheet, from Morton Street at the top to the bottom edge south of Park Avenue. On the west side West Park Avenue crosses the sheet, with Morton running north from it and turning east to Main Street at the head of the sheet. On the east side Cliff Street, marked as an arbitrary name, and Park Avenue, which leaves Main Street at an angle towards the south-east, divide the large blocks numbered 4, 5 and 6. Most of the area is open lots with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings and outbuildings. Commerce is concentrated on Main Street: a general store and post office and a second general store near West Park Avenue, the Oakhurst Inn with a saloon opposite, a meat shop, a pool room, a cobbler, a shop, a blacksmith drawn in green, a hay and feed store, a Masonic Hall and another hall. A large two-and-a-half-storey building on the corner of West Park Avenue is marked vacant, and a carpenter's shop stands on Morton. An elevated water tank of 10,000 gallons stands at the east end of Cliff. The upper right corner carries the town title with its fire-protection notes: population 500, no steam or hand engines, no independent hose cart, poor water facilities, prevailing wind west. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed in the blank eastern blocks, and a heavy line cuts off the lower left corner for the inset of Lake Avenue.
notes: Main Street (Monmouth Road) is today's Monmouth Road (County Route 71).
Morton, drawn as an L from West Park Avenue north and then east to Main Street, follows today's Brown Place; Marcy Place, a later stub, is not drawn.
Cliff is labelled '(Arbitrary)', a name assigned by the map maker; it is today's Laird Street.
West Park Avenue and Park Avenue keep their names; Park Avenue was drawn 35 ft wide.
Main is printed as 'MAIN (MONMOUTH R'D)'; the street names column lists both names.
Town notes printed on the sheet: population 500; no steam and no hand engines; no independent hose cart; water facilities poor; prevailing wind west.
The corner of Brown Place's two legs did not fit the other control (about 5 m off) and was left out of the fit.

Printed sheet 73 of New Jersey Coast vol. 1 (canvas label 9999997). Scale 60 ft to an inch; north arrow points straight up (fitted rotation about 12 degrees: probably magnetic north). Two parts: part 1 main map along Main Street (Monmouth Road) from Morton (Brown Place) south past West Park Avenue, Cliff (Laird Street) and Park Avenue; part 2 lower-left inset of Main Street at Lake Avenue, north of part 1 and overlapping its top row of lots. Control: street junctions along Monmouth Road plus parcel block corners at lot lines (no junction off Main survives in the area).

sheet-9999997-2.description: An inset in the lower left corner of the Oakhurst sheet (sheet 73 of the 1907 New Jersey Coast volume one), boxed off by a heavy line and drawn at the same 60 feet to an inch and orientation as the main map. It shows the west side of Main Street, labelled Monmouth Road, north of the main map, where Lake Avenue runs west from Main Street across the inset. The inset reaches north to a row of lots marked 'Pond beyond' and south to the top row of lots of the main map, which it repeats; Main Street is drawn only to its west edge, with 'Vacant beyond' lettered along it. Morton runs north from the bottom of the inset towards Lake but is drawn only south of a lot line about midway. The blocks are divided into narrow house lots numbered along Lake (15 to 23 on the north side, 24 to 30 on the south) and hold one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings; there are no shops, works or public buildings. A small north arrow sits in the block north of Lake. Lettering at the left edge reads 'No exposure', and one lot is marked '55 ft to Fr. D.', giving the distance to the nearest frame dwelling beyond the drawn area. The sheet number 73 is repeated at the bottom edge, where the inset joins the main map.
notes: Lake is today's Lake Avenue; Main Street (Monmouth Road) is today's Monmouth Road.
Morton here is the northern continuation of the Morton of the main map, today's Brown Place, which now ends south of Lake Avenue.
The bottom row of lots repeats the top row of the main map; two points of that overlap were carried from part 1 into this part's control.
Printed 'Pond beyond' along the north edge and 'Vacant beyond' along Main Street.
